images.caption: Icebergs, Ilulissat, Greenland
images.desc: Off Greenland's west coast, enormous icebergs drift through the cold waters, creating a landscape that's constantly changing. Many originate from the nearby Jakobshavn Glacier, one of the world's fastest and most active glaciers. The surrounding Ilulissat Icefjord, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lies about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle. Here, towering blocks of ice break away and begin their slow journey towards the open sea, forming one of Greenland's most remarkable natural sights.

images.caption: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
images.desc: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by ancient Greeks and long connected to the Italian royal House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, that layered past remains visible throughout the coastal city in the south of France, where old-world architecture meets the blue Mediterranean waters and sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.

images.title: Info
images.caption: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway
images.desc: Off the coast of Kvaløya in Troms, Northern Norway, humpback whales move through the cold Arctic waters in search of a proper feast. They visit this region during the winter months, following migrating herring into the fjords. Humpbacks are famous for bubble-net feeding, a remarkable hunting technique in which whales blow rings of bubbles to corral fish before lunging upwards, open-mouthed, to catch their prey. In today's image, a humpback slips beneath the icy waves under a glowing pastel sky, capturing a moment of tranquility in Norway's wild north.

images.title: Info
images.caption: Coast redwoods near Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
images.desc: Step into this peaceful redwood forest in Victoria, Australia, and the outside world can suddenly feel very far away. Coast redwoods (Sequoia sempervirens) tower overhead, forming a leafy canopy above the forest floor. These impressive trees have grown into one of the region's most distinctive woodland sights. With their tall trunks, deep green foliage and tranquil surroundings, the redwoods create an inviting place to wander, slow down and enjoy the quiet beauty of the forest.

images.copyright: Pair of barn owls (© Zahoor Salmi/Getty Images)
images.title: Info
images.caption: Pair of barn owls
images.desc: These barn owls, bathed in evening light, are waiting for the hunt to begin. As night falls, these birds of prey swoop into action, listening for tiny movements in grass or leaves made by mice and voles. Their heart-shaped faces help funnel sound into some of the sharpest ears in the animal kingdom. This allows them to locate their prey with pinpoint precision in the dark before swooping silently, their soft feathers muffling their approach. In autumn, young barn owls strike out to find their own territories. As the nights grow longer, you might spot them earlier in the evening, gliding over fields in search of supper.

images.title: Info
images.caption: Trail of the Cedars, Glacier National Park, Montana, USA
images.desc: Sometimes, the best way to clear your head is to step outside. Today's image features the Trail of the Cedars, part of more than 1,100 kilometres of hiking trails in Glacier National Park, Montana, in the northwestern USA. Its 1.4-kilometre loop includes a raised boardwalk that cuts a path through western red cedar and hemlock trees. The park boasts routes for all abilities, taking in alpine lakes, wildflower meadows, mountain passes and wilderness stretching to the Canadian border.

images.copyright: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument, New Mexico, USA (© Chiara Salvadori/Getty Images)
images.title: Info
images.caption: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument, New Mexico, USA
images.desc: Incredible views and rock-solid foundations are part of the charm of these ancient dwellings, set into the cliffside in New Mexico, USA. Nomads had long used the natural caves above Cliff Dweller Creek as temporary shelter, but it was the Native American Mogollon people who made them their home. Archaeologists believe they created dozens of rooms inside five alcoves in the 1270s and 1280s. Up to 15 families lived here at any one time, raising children, making pottery and overlooking the fertile Gila River valley where they grew crops and hunted wildlife. For reasons unknown, the Mogollon people moved on around 1300, leaving behind one of the American Southwest's most important archaeological sites.

images.copyright: Frozen azalea with red leaves (© avoferten/Shutterstock)
images.title: Info
images.caption: Frozen azalea with red leaves
images.desc: As colder weather sets in, ice crystals form on the leaves of evergreen shrubs, like this azalea. Long gone are the pinks, orange and yellows of their spring blooms, but a new colourful display awaits, as their green leaves turn shades of red and purple. For the plants, the new pigments protect their leaves as temperatures drop, but for gardeners, they create a vibrant autumnal display, framed in white frost. When spring arrives, new growth will restore the shrub's green leaves, and the colourful cycle begins anew.
